sections.title: Galaxy Pack identity
paragraphs: Galaxy Scout is an Outfit from the Galaxy Pack set, introduced during Chapter 2, Season 3. The community record associates it with the Nucleus Back Bling. Its star-filled appearance is a visual theme, not a documented character class. Keep the Outfit, its matching accessories and the differently named Galaxy Grappler as separate catalog records when planning a cosmetic combination.

sections.title: Historical reward and current shop
paragraphs: Epic announced early access through the July 25–26, 2020 Android Galaxy Cup and said the Outfit would later reach the Item Shop. That competition is historical, not an active free-unlock method. A stored shop offer is also only a snapshot: use the official shop to check whether it is available today and whether the displayed price belongs to a bundle.

sections.title: Equip and inspect
paragraphs: After ownership is confirmed, open Locker from the lobby, select Character and choose the Outfit, then return to view your avatar. For a useful visual check, compare the front and back with any Back Bling you plan to use. GameBreak recommends inspecting the actual preview rather than deciding from the small catalog icon alone.

sections.title: Appearance, not a combat upgrade
paragraphs: Epic states that Outfits do not change hitbox size or improve competitive performance. Galaxy Scout therefore has no Outfit-based damage, shield or movement bonus to list. If your goal is to improve a Battle Royale result, use a mechanics guide alongside this cosmetic record; buying the appearance does not replace practice with the weapons and movement in your selected mode.

history.label: July–August 2020
history.detail: Epic’s July announcement documents the original Galaxy Cup route; the community catalog records the Item Shop release on August 1, 2020. Neither date predicts the next shop rotation.

sections.title: Event Horizon set
paragraphs: Galaxy Grappler is an Outfit in the Event Horizon set, distinct from Galaxy Scout and from the Grappler gameplay item. Its matching Hands of the Galaxy is a Back Bling, while Galaxy Starblades is a Pickaxe cosmetic. Keeping these categories separate prevents a cosmetic bundle from being presented as a weapon loadout with invented combat statistics.

sections.title: Tournament origin and rotation
paragraphs: The original Galaxy Cup 2.0 ran on August 29, 2021 for eligible Android players. Epic announced the Outfit, Back Bling and wrap as early rewards and confirmed later Item Shop availability. Those tournament instructions describe a past event. Today, check the current official offer and its included items; an old event article does not grant the Outfit to an account.

sections.title: Inspect the matching pieces
paragraphs: Equip the owned Outfit through the Locker’s Character section and check your avatar after returning. Inspect any matching accessory separately instead of assuming that everything shown in promotional art is included in a single-item purchase. GameBreak’s visual suggestion is to preview the full combination in motion and check how the Back Bling sits against the character’s silhouette.

sections.title: Reactive accessory, cosmetic effect
paragraphs: The official bundle page describes Hands of the Galaxy as reactive to eliminations. This is an accessory effect, not an ability that increases elimination damage. Epic’s Outfit guidance also says cosmetic appearance does not change hitbox size or competitive performance. This record therefore separates visual reactions from gameplay powers and does not assign a fabricated skill tree to the Outfit.

history.label: August–September 2021
history.detail: Galaxy Cup 2.0 introduced early access in August; the community catalog records a September 5, 2021 shop release in Chapter 2, Season 7. This is release history, not proof of current availability.

sections.title: Stealth Syndicate Outfit
paragraphs: Midnight Ops belongs to the Stealth Syndicate set and first appeared in the original Season 3 period. This page describes the Battle Royale Outfit, not the Save the World hero Undercover Vaughn. A shared visual model or similar name does not transfer a hero’s abilities into Battle Royale. Use the exact Outfit record when comparing appearances or checking your collection.

sections.title: An Item Shop cosmetic
paragraphs: The community catalog records it as an Item Shop Outfit with a historical single-item price of 1,200 V-Bucks. That is reference information, not a live offer or a promise of its next return. Read the official shop’s current price and availability before making a decision, especially when a site card shows a provider date from an earlier rotation.

sections.title: Locker and visual checks
paragraphs: Choose the owned Outfit through the lobby Locker’s Character section, then return to see the selected avatar. GameBreak suggests viewing it with your intended Back Bling and Pickaxe cosmetic before a match. Look at the complete silhouette, rather than treating the isolated portrait as the whole design. This is a styling workflow, not a required purchase recommendation.

sections.title: No stealth statistic
paragraphs: The name and dark visual theme do not supply a stealth skill, reduced hitbox or movement bonus. Epic states that Outfits are cosmetic and do not improve competitive performance. For practical play, evaluate your position, cover and selected mode’s mechanics separately. There is no verified character biography or combat skill tree in these sources, so this dossier does not invent either.

history.label: 30 March 2018
history.detail: The community record dates the first release to March 30, 2018 and associates the asset with update v3.40. Shop appearance counts and last-seen dates are deliberately not fixed here because they change with later rotations.
